papers.title: Wave as Disturbance and Signal in a Physics-Informed Framework for Shallow Water Bathymetry
papers.abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) commonly treats the sea surface as a source of radiometric disturbance, although the same surface wave field can also contain water depth information through gravity wave propagation. This article presents a Wave-Aware Physics-Informed Neural Network (WA-PINN) that represents these two roles within a unified shallow water bathymetry framework. The optical geometry stream combines Sentinel-2 multispectral observations with seafloor geometry. The disturbance stream converts European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis Version 5 (ERA5) wind forcing into Mean Square Slope (MSS) through the Cox–Munk relationship and introduces a roughness-dependent sunglint contribution into the optical physics constraint. The signal stream retrieves local wavelength, propagation direction, and wave celerity from Sentinel-2 surface texture and constrains predicted depth with the finite depth gravity wave dispersion relation. A Wave Validity Factor (WVF) controls the influence of the dispersion constraint according to the coherence and physical plausibility of the retrieved wave field. The three streams are fused in a shared depth predictor constrained by supervised depth loss, optical physics loss, and wave dispersion physics loss. The framework is demonstrated over Culebra, St. Thomas, and St. John in the northeastern Caribbean Sea. The complete Dual Role model reaches an overall Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1.21 m, a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) 0.77 m, and an R2 of 0.96. Relative to the Slope Aware configuration, the Disturbance and Signal models reduce RMSE by 15.7% and 12.8%, while the complete model reduces RMSE by 29.7%. The disturbance contribution increases under stronger wind forcing, whereas the signal contribution increases with WVF. Depth-dependent RMSE increases from 0.82 m at 0 to 5 m to 1.58 m at 20 to 30 m. These results illustrate the intended complementarity between correcting wave-induced optical contamination and exploiting wave propagation as an additional depth constraint.

papers.title: Multivariable control of large-scale pressurized water reactor based on LPV-MPC algorithm over a wide operating range
papers.abstract: For energy conservation, large-scale Pressurized Water Reactors (PWRs) are required to participate in grid peak shaving. Compared to traditional PID control, Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithm offers advantages in handling multivariable control problems. However, PWR systems exhibit strong nonlinearity under wide-range operation, limiting conventional MPC performance. Therefore, Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) models, valued for their nonlinear approximation capability and low computational cost, are employed in nonlinear MPC. This paper proposes an LPV model-based MPC algorithm to enhance the control of a nonlinear HPR1000 model. An iterative optimization strategy is adopted for LPV model identification: first, initial local models are identified using the asymptotic method; then, parameters of the weighting functions are estimated via least squares; finally, the LPV model is optimized iteratively based on the total data. The local models demonstrate good performance in both time-domain and frequency-domain validation. The optimized LPV model shows high similarity to the plant’s step responses at both high and low loads, confirming its suitability for MPC controller. The LPV-MPC is compared with both the original control system and a fixed-model MPC (F-MPC) through test scenarios at 100 % and 50 % FP. The results indicate that the LPV-MPC controller offers comparable performance at 100 % FP, but exhibits faster regulation speed and stronger capability in suppressing SG water level fluctuations at 50 % FP. The comparison with F-MPC demonstrates that the LPV-MPC possesses stronger adaptability and robustness. Meanwhile, a large-scale transition scenario was implemented. The comparative analysis confirms that the LPV-MPC controller possesses superior load-following performance.

papers.title: Multi-Level Text Alignment for Interpretable and Uncertainty-Aware Time Series Forecasting with LLMs
papers.abstract: Adapting large language models (LLMs) for time series forecasting introduces unique challenges due to the mismatch between continuous time series tokens and the discrete word tokens LLMs are trained on. While LLMs have shown success on natural language tasks, aligning time series tokens with the semantic space of LLMs while preserving both accuracy and interpretability remains an open problem. Existing reprogramming and prompt-based approaches often generate word embeddings that are misaligned with or semantically irrelevant to the corresponding time series. For example, a segment with an increasing trend may be mapped to words like ”mirror” or ”keyboard”, which makes them hard to interpret. To bridge the gap, we propose MLTA-LLM, a Multi-Level Text Alignment framework for time series forecasting with LLMs. MLTA-LLM decomposes time series into trend, seasonal, and residual components, each of which is aligned with semantic anchor embeddings or text prototype embeddings. This component-specific alignment forces the LLM to process time series data through structured, interpretable representations. In addition, we integrate conformal prediction to provide statistically rigorous prediction intervals for uncertainty quantification. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that MLTA-LLM not only improves forecasting accuracy over state-of-the-art baselines but also yields more interpretable representations and better-calibrated uncertainty estimates.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Bioengineering: Innovations, Challenges, and Future Directions: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming bioengineering, with applications ranging from diagnosis and biomedical imaging to wearable technologies, rehabilitation, biomaterials, biofabrication, and digital twins. This narrative review aims to examine the major innovations, challenges, and future directions of AI-enabled bioengineering, with particular attention to its clinical and translational development. The literature was searched in Scopus and PubMed, with emphasis on systematic reviews and meta-analyses and consideration of other relevant secondary literature across the main bioengineering domains. A total of 57 secondary publications were included in the principal evidence base. The review process was additionally informed by the ANDJ Narrative Review Checklist and an established qualification and scoring methodology applied to the selected secondary literature. The reviewed evidence shows a broad expansion of AI applications and increasing integration of intelligent technologies into bioengineering systems. However, important challenges remain, particularly regarding data quality and representativeness, validation and generalizability, reproducibility, safety, human oversight, ethical responsibility, equity, and regulatory requirements. Future developments are expected to increasingly involve multimodal, adaptive, connected, and human-centered systems integrating AI with sensing technologies, robotics, digital twins, and longitudinal data. Overall, AI-enabled bioengineering is progressing from promising technological applications toward increasingly integrated and translational systems. Its successful evolution will depend on combining technological innovation with robust clinical evidence, responsible development, and appropriate ethical and regulatory frameworks.

papers.title: Bayesian Inverse Optimisation under Uncertainty Posterior Inference for Hidden Decision Objectives
papers.abstract: Inverse optimization seeks the hidden objective that explains observed decisions, yet existing methods typically recover a single objective and ignore uncertainty in the underlying preferences. We develop a Bayesian framework that represents the unknown objective by a posterior distribution, combining a boundedrationality choice model with prior information to quantify uncertainty directly. We establish geometric conditions for identifiability, prove posterior consistency, derive the optimal n−1/2, contraction rate, obtain a Bernstein–von Mises approximation, and present a finite-sample concentration bound together with a robust fractional posterior for misspecified behavioural models. Posterior inference is performed using gradient-based Markov chain Monte Carlo and a Laplace approximation. Simulation studies demonstrate accurate recovery under noisy, misspecified, nonlinear, and high-dimensional settings, while a controlled clinical example illustrates uncertainty quantification in hidden decision preferences. The proposed framework extends inverse optimization from point estimation to statistically principled uncertainty quantification, providing a rigorous foundation for learning decision objectives from imperfect observations.

papers.title: Estimation of aggregate flexibility regions for distributed flexible resources using limited information
papers.abstract: Distributed flexible resources (DFRs) can support power-system operation only if aggregators can report their flexibility regions as operating conditions change. Existing aggregation methods generally require detailed device-level states, which may be unavailable, as well as repeated online optimization. This paper proposes a limited-information physics-informed neural network (PINN) for estimating aggregate flexibility regions of DFRs. Its inputs are low-dimensional operating-condition descriptors, and its output is a feasibility-oriented representative polyhedral region conditioned on those descriptors. Physical feasibility and boundary tightness are embedded through support- and projection-based errors and differentiable active-hyperplane residuals, enabling training without precomputed ground-truth flexibility-region labels. The proposed pretraining, full-network training, and loss-weight scheduling scheme prioritizes physical feasibility while retaining boundary tightness. papers.title: Size and geometry effects on the flow-rate–torque trade-off of a drainage impeller in a submerged mechanical defoamer
papers.abstract: Abstract Rotating drainage impellers must balance suction-driven flow against shaft loading, yet which geometric parameters govern this flow-rate–torque trade-off remains poorly established. This work addresses this question for the drainage impeller of a submerged mechanical defoamer, focusing on the single-phase hydrodynamics underlying froth capture rather than directly modelling foam rupture. Thirty configurations spanning four geometric parameters — blade number Z, impeller diameter D, impeller height H and blade outlet angle β — were generated by maximin orthogonal Latin hypercube sampling and evaluated by three-dimensional steady-state CFD for drainage flow rate and torque. Gaussian-process surrogates with leave-one-out cross-validation then supported conditional-response analysis, Sobol sensitivity indices and surrogate-based multi-objective Bayesian optimization. The results show that impeller diameter dominates the dimensional responses, with first-order Sobol indices of 0.91 for flow rate and 0.96 for torque. After dimensional normalization removes the leading size-scaling effects, diameter still governs the flow coefficient, whereas impeller height emerges as the principal secondary factor for the torque coefficient, indicating that size mainly sets the operating point while the residual geometry modulates the normalized loading. A representative Pareto compromise design (Z = 8, D = 81.11 mm, H = 30 mm, β = 120°) was verified by CFD within 6% of the surrogate predictions; relative to the original impeller it raises the flow rate by 25.5%, a gain attributable mainly to the enlarged diameter rather than to improve dimensionless flow capacity. Water experiments at 1000 rev/min confirmed the CFD predictions for both impellers, with flow-rate deviations within 5% and torque deviations within 10%. Flow-field analysis relates the higher throughput to an enlarged suction-related low-pressure region, smoother blade-passage flow and reduced local wake dissipation. The framework provides a practical basis for drainage-impeller design and, more generally, for separating size and geometry effects in CFD-based optimization under limited simulation budgets.

papers.title: AI-Guided Clinical Image Interpretation System for Precision Treatment Planning
papers.abstract: Radiological examinations increasingly leverage artificial intelligence to enhance diagnostic performance by compensating for expertise shortages, particularly in specialized interpretation. Despite academic AI models achieving compelling accuracy, adoption remains low. An objective, evidence-based examination of AI-guided clinical image interpretation seeks to expose the underlying reasons. The primary challenge lies not in accuracy but in fully automated analysis, especially for multimodal and multidimensional datasets. Introduction of uncertainty measures, image explainability, and real-world data reduce recognition to a decisive-supporting role—helping radiologists to detect previously unnoticed abnormalities—or even to precautionary analysis. Patients requesting precision medicine and therapy planning—and those at high risk of neglected pathology—stand to gain the greatest benefit. Relevant AI architecture considers imaging cues suitable for precision medicine or requiring additional methods to obtain interpretable images. Successful performance testing against an external, hidden reference dataset promotes vital user trust. Machine learning achieves best results where all potentially pathological abnormalities are identified and their presence virtually guaranteed, as in multi-class recognition. Data scarcity, however, impedes clinically relevant solutions. Explainability, essential for medical applications and clinical acceptance, extends simply beyond clinical decision support to provide saliency maps and, better still, clinically meaningful image regions or qualities. Attention maps may even bring a form of rule-based reasoning within reach. Clinical integration that reproduces the technical conditions under which model diagnostic measures are calculated raises the challenge of uncertainty quantification—a necessary condition for clinical decision support. Convolutional neural networks trained for photo-quality classification, par excellence supervised image quality assessment, provide the basic cues for uncertainty quantification. Imaging acquisition, modality, and systems are also defined in terms of current PACS/EPIC systems. PE, pre-symptomatic examination or precautionary examination, is defined as a patient-user group prepared to cover the cost of an examination with lower diagnostic accuracy and a high level of uncertainty.

papers.title: A structure-preserving potential-Logphi framework for forward approximation and coefficient identification of extended CBS-like nonlinear wave equations
papers.abstract: Abstract The extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff-like equation is a representative $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlinear evolution equation in mathematical physics. For coupled formulations of such nonlinear systems, conventional multi-output physics-informed neural networks may not explicitly preserve intrinsic compatibility relations between physical fields. In this work, a structure-preserving Potential-Logphi PINN is developed for the forward approximation and inverse coefficient identification of the extended CBS-like equation. In the proposed framework, the neural network represents a scalar potential $v_\theta(x,y,t)$, from which the coupled fields are reconstructed by automatic differentiation as $u_\theta=\partial_x v_\theta$ and $w_\theta=\partial_y v_\theta$. This potential representation naturally satisfies the compatibility relation $u_y-w_x=0$. Five exact-solution benchmarks with lump, soliton, periodic, and mixed interaction structures are investigated. Numerical results show that the proposed framework accurately reconstructs complex localized wave fields and provides stable derivative information for coefficient identification. Across three independent runs in the matched comparison, the proposed Potential-Logphi formulation achieves the lowest mean relative-$L_2$ errors for both coupled fields among all five evaluated model formulations. The Potential-Logphi formulation therefore provides a structure-consistent neural approach for learning coupled nonlinear wave equations with tau-function-based solution structures.

papers.title: Deep-Learning Error Correction of Regional Significant Wave Height Forecasts
papers.abstract: Deep-learning post-processing can correct systematic errors in numerical wave forecasts, but its reliability under high-wave conditions remains unclear. We develop an error-correction framework in which deep networks predict the full future error trajectory of operational forecasts, and compare three architectures, a pure LSTM, a pure Transformer and a hybrid LSTM–Transformer, tuned identically with Bayesian optimization, using hourly observations from six buoys in the Bohai Sea and Yellow Sea over 2023–2025. On the full test sample all models improve the 72 h forecasts by 15.37% to 23.93% in RMSE, with the hybrid model attaining the lowest pooled RMSE; on the high-wave subset with SWH above 1.5 m, however, all three degrade the forecast, increasing RMSE by 7.58% to 9.05%. An exact decomposition of the squared-error change shows that fluctuation-capturing skill remains intact while the degradation is driven by the mean term: trained on samples dominated by low and moderate waves, the correctors learn a globally averaged adjustment whose sign opposes the reversed raw bias at high waves. Neither loss reweighting nor filtered training resolves this degradation at the 72 h horizon. Shortening the horizon to 24 h restores positive skill, with RMSE reductions of 4.43% to 7.88%, and reverses the ranking in favor of the pure LSTM. These findings indicate that architecture rankings are horizon-dependent, and they are consistent with the interpretation that extreme-condition skill is limited by the information content of the predictors rather than by model capacity.

For the learned controllers, annual performance is reported as mean ± standard deviation across four independent retraining runs, while generalisation is assessed separately using a seasonally distributed four-month temporal hold-out. The Hybrid achieved a mean annual cost of $9353.49 ± 122.63, a 20.91% reduction relative to the deterministic rule-based baseline. papers.title: AI-guided extraction of plant-derived bioactives for edible packaging films
papers.abstract: The increasing concern for plastic pollution and the rising demand for sustainable food packaging, have accelerated research on edible packaging films fortified with bioactive compounds from plants. Phytochemicals such as flavonoids, terpenoids and polyphenols confer antioxidant, antimicrobial and functional properties to improve food safety, maintain quality and extend shelf-life. However, conventional extraction methods such as Soxhlet, maceration and solvent extraction have disadvantages of high solvent and energy consumption, low selectivity and extraction efficiency and thermal degradation of bioactives. Furthermore, the nonlinear relationships among the extraction variables are complex and limit the performance of conventional statistical optimization methods. This review critically examines the integration of conventional statistical optimization tools, especially response surface methodology (RSM) and design of experiments (DoE), with machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) strategies for advanced green extraction processes such as microwave-assisted, ultrasound-assisted, enzyme-assisted, supercritical fluid, pulsed electric field, and pressurized liquid extraction. RSM/DoE helps in systematic experimental design and optimization of processes, whereas ML methods, including Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest (RF), and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS), enable data-assisted prediction of nonlinear relationships. DL architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), autoencoders (AE), transformers, and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), support complex and high-dimensional datasets when sufficient training data are available; However, their significance in edible packaging research, where datasets are relatively small and heterogeneous, must be addressed in terms of model complexity, overfitting and validation robustness. It further evaluates AI-guided incorporation of plant bioactives into edible packaging through optimized encapsulation, prediction of mechanical and barrier properties, controlled release behavior, safety assessment, and sustainability evaluation. AI-assisted and hybrid models have demonstrated, in various reported studies, enhanced predictive accuracy and optimization efficacy compared with conventional response surface methodology in terms of extraction yield, solvent use, energy demand and experimental trials. However, the limitations of standardised datasets, computational complexity, regulatory issues and lack of large-scale validation restrict the applications in industry. The reviewed literature still provides limited evidence directly linking mechanical, barrier and release properties, as well as safety outcomes such as migration, to ML-based modeling and optimization. Formulation-specific experimental validation is therefore still required. Future advances in explainable AI frameworks, harmonized databases, industrial-scale studies and multidisciplinary collaboration will be crucial for the commercialization of intelligent and sustainable edible packaging systems. Further scale-up studies are needed before these approaches can be considered viable for industrial application. Their translation will depend on process reproducibility, regulatory acceptance, sufficiently large and representative datasets, appropriate computational resources, formulation-specific testing, mechanism-informed modeling and uncertainty quantification. Any proposed formulation will also require independent experimental validation, together with food-safety and shelf-life studies, before it can be accepted for food-contact applications.

papers.title: AI-driven analysis of bioconvective Casson–Williamson penta-hybrid nanofluid flow over exponentially stretching surface using ANN and physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the bioconvective flow of a Casson–Williamson penta-hybrid nanofluid across an exponentially stretching permeable surface. The analysis accounts for the joint effects of a magnetic field, porous medium, thermal radiation, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, heat generation and chemical reaction on the transport behavior. Design/methodology/approach The physical problem is described through the governing partial differential equations for momentum, energy, concentration and the movement of motile microorganisms. Suitable similarity transformations reduce these dimensional equations into a coupled set of nonlinear ordinary differential equations, which are then solved numerically using the bvp4c technique in MATLAB. To complement the numerical work, an artificial neural network based on the Levenberg–Marquardt Algorithm (ANN-LMA) and a physics-informed NN (PINN) framework are constructed to predict the Nusselt number across mono-hybrid, tri-hybrid, tetra-hybrid and penta-hybrid nanoparticle systems. Findings The results reveal that increasing the magnetic field, porosity, Casson and Williamson parameters slows the fluid motion, while thermal radiation, Brownian motion, thermophoresis and heat generation raise the temperature within the boundary layer. The density of motile microorganisms falls as the Lewis and Peclet numbers grow. A comparative assessment shows that the penta-hybrid nanofluid outperforms the mono-hybrid, tri-hybrid and tetra-hybrid systems in heat transfer, mass transport and microorganism flux, a consequence of the stronger interaction among the dispersed nanoparticles. Originality/value Both the ANN-LMA and PINN models achieve very low mean squared error values and align closely with the numerical solutions, capturing the heat transfer response with notable precision. This work highlights the practical importance of penta-hybrid nanofluids and neural-network-based prediction tools for advanced thermal engineering and bioconvective transport applications. The ANN-LMA and PINN models achieved correlation coefficients close to unity (R≈1) and MSEs of the order of 10−10, confirming excellent predictive accuracy.

papers.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Ship Maneuvering Dynamics via Control-Aware Hankel-DMDc and Mode Attribution
papers.abstract: Accurate data-driven identification and long-term forecasting of surface ship motions in realistic ocean environments are essential for advanced autonomous navigation and predictive control systems. However, robust system identification in such conditions remains challenging due to high-frequency wave-induced disturbances, which contaminate measured signals and may contribute to error accumulation in recursive forecasting. This paper proposes a control- and wave-aware data-driven framework for modeling and prediction of ship maneuvering dynamics in stochastic wave environments. The approach integrates Hankel dynamic mode decomposition with control (Hankel-DMDc) with a spectral Mode Attribution Layer that characterizes modal associations with commanded control inputs and measured wave excitation. A dual-criterion selection rule, based on the Wave Energy Projection (WEP) and Control Correlation Index (CCI), is introduced to characterize and separate maneuvering-related and wave-associated modal content without relying on a predefined physical model. The framework is evaluated on a multidimensional ship-motion dataset from the DaRUS repository, using routine maneuvering trajectories for model identification and independent out-of-distribution test trajectories for prediction evaluation. One-step prediction analysis indicates high local accuracy, particularly for rotational states, while recursive multi-step forecasting shows gradual error growth over a 200-step prediction horizon. A quantitative comparison with unfiltered Hankel-DMDc, conventional Butterworth filtering, and direct wave-input modeling further shows that the proposed framework retains predictive performance comparable to direct Hankel-DMDc for the present dataset, while providing explicit modal attribution and wave/maneuvering characterization. The identified discrete-time operator also exhibits a spectral radius below unity, while no rapid divergence is observed over the evaluated recursive prediction horizon. The proposed methodology provides an interpretable data-driven framework for modeling marine systems, with potential applicability to control-oriented system identification, predictive modeling, autonomous navigation, and Model Predictive Control (MPC).
